title: A patch whose JSON Pointer has 320,000 tokens names no location and must be refused as a path error
notes: The document is `x: 1`. The patch removes the location `/a/a/a/...` with 320,000 tokens (a 640 KB pointer). A pointer is evaluated token by token from the root (RFC 6901 section 4), and the document has no member `a`, so the location does not exist and `remove` must fail (RFC 6902 section 4.2: the target location MUST exist). The only acceptable outcome is the path error, reported within the bounds: a patch from an untrusted party can carry a pointer of any length, and a library whose cost is more than linear in the number of tokens, or that builds a message or a hint from the whole pointer, fails on time or memory. A failed patch is not applied (RFC 6902 section 5), and the kit holds every refused patch to leaving the document byte for byte as it was (docs/edit-semantics.md, Refusals); the case states it. A refusal as a limit error, from a size cap on the patch, is also correct.

provenance.reference: A pointer error that rebuilt a hint from the whole pointer for each token, so the cost grew with the square of the length.
